messages:
sam: heads-up — noticed a weird wide-role binding in the sandbox cluster, possible serviceaccount token exposure from gpu-pool nodes. unsure if it's a bug or we misconfigured rolebindings.
anika: can you paste the RoleBinding/ClusterRoleBinding? sandbox RBAC has been in flux after the dev sandbox refactor.
sam: here's the binding I found in audit logs: `kubectl get clusterrolebinding sandbox-devs -o yaml` -> shows subjects: group: system:serviceaccounts, roleRef: cluster-admin
kevin: whoa. that would grant cluster-admin to all serviceaccounts in the cluster if it's scoped to system:serviceaccounts. that smells like the leftover from the old onboarding script.
jordan: timeline? did any deploys or sea changes happen recently that could've added that?
sam: it appears ~2 days ago. audit-bot shows a `kubectl apply -f` from a CI job by `sandbox-onboard` service account.
security-bot: alert: possible privilege escalation path: serviceaccounts in gpu namespace may be able to impersonate workloads and access KMS keys via node-level agents.
lee: quick mitigation: patch the ClusterRoleBinding to remove `system:serviceaccounts` and replace with explicit namespaces / groups. but we should avoid blunt RBAC edits at 3am.
maria: agree. propose staged approach: (1) revoke tokens for suspicious sa, (2) create least-privilege roles for sandbox workloads, (3) run dry-run policy to detect breakages, (4) apply in canary ns.
sam: for revocation — we can't revoke existing projected tokens easily unless we rotate secrets or restart pods. suggestion: taint nodes or cordon gpu-pool nodes while we triage.
kevin: alternative: use `kubectl delete secret -n <ns> $(kubectl get sa <sa> -o jsonpath='{.secrets[*].name}')` to force token remounts. also set `automountServiceAccountToken: false` on daemonsets that don't need it.
anika: will open a quick PR to add `automountServiceAccountToken: false` in our gpu-pool node-provisioner pod spec and a webhook to deny projected tokens for non-approved pods.
security-bot: note: KMS access logs show two decrypts from a node in gpu-pool around the same time as the apply. need to map which workloads used those decrypts.
audit-bot: audit entries: `user=sandbox-onboard-sa, verb=create, resource=clusterrolebinding` + `sourceIP=10.240.7.12` -> correlate with CI runner IP.
jordan: CI runner token compromised? or pipeline misconfigured to run as high-priv SA. check pipeline job definition immediately.
lee: tagging for vuln triage: assign to #vuln-triage, set severity=p0 if we can't confirm scope within 4h.
maria: I've created the vuln ticket and added steps. PR drafted for RBAC lock-down: change binding to namespace-scoped RoleBinding for `sandbox-admins` only and remove cluster-admin privileges.
sam: also recommend adding a guard in admission: deny creation of ClusterRoleBinding that references `system:serviceaccounts` or cluster-admin role via our admission controller.\nkevin: good. to be safe, rotate KMS envelope keys used by CI integration and revoke the CI service principal until we validate.
anika: patch plan: 1) snapshot current clusterrolebinding and audit; 2) create namespace-scoped roles; 3) apply deny webhook in staging; 4) canary apply to `sandbox-dev` ns; 5) full rollout. I'll run the dry-run and post results.
sam: any objections to cordoning the affected gpu nodes for 30m to contain? will impact workloads but gives us breathing room.
maria: +1 from sec and ops. coordinate with oncall.
oncall-bot: paging oncall: incident declared (sandbox-ksa-escape). oncall: please ACK and coordinate node cordon if approved.
kevin: ACK. cordon scheduled in 10m, will notify impacted teams.
jordan: follow-up: we should also add an automated periodic audit rule that flags clusterrolebindings with broad subject groups and alerts to eng-security.
lee: I'll add metric/alarm in the console (RBAC anomalies dashboard) and tie to slack alert.
anika: PR merged to staging (link: https://git.internal/r/PR/2345) — dry-run shows 2 pods would be impacted, both test workloads. proceeding with canary.
sam: thanks everyone. keep thread updated with token rotation timeline and KMS key rotation status.
security-bot: action items summary: revoke ci sa tokens, rotate KMS keys, patch automount, remove wide clusterrolebinding, add admission deny, add rbac alerting. assigned to anika/kevin/maria.
maria: putting remediation ETA at 6 hours. filing postmortem template after stabilization.
anika: will also add a follow-up to review onboarding scripts that create these bindings. likely root cause is deprecated bootstrap script.
kevin: after mitigation, recommend run `kubectl auth can-i --as system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa> create clusterrolebinding` checks across namespaces and fail CI if any can.
sam: closing loop: please paste final verification steps and tag this thread when done. thanks :thumbsup:
